rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 3 (score 361.4, best so far) finished all 20 oval trials, but every s-bend and slalom trial still ended off track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m. Checking the contract, the off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4). For body_width 0.18 that is 0.06 m, not the 0.0575 m I assumed in iteration 2. So the robot exceeds the limit by only 2 to 3 mm on the bends, and body_width cannot help because it is already at its useful ceiling.

What the iterations show: (a) Iteration 1 to 3 comparison: lowering base_speed from 1.3 to 1.1 with the wider sensor span made s-bend progress fall (0.27 to 0.22) and slalom progress fall (0.18 to 0.10). Speed overshoot is therefore not the main cause of bend failure. The robot is too slow to correct, not too fast. (b) Iteration 2 widened the sensor span, raised sensor_size to 0.016, raised kp to 3.0 and kd to 1.0 together. The oval finish rate fell to 0.55 and control_effort rose, so the larger footprint and higher kp are the likely cause. The wider span alone was never tested cleanly. (c) Iteration 3 has the widest span with sensor_size 0.012 and a clean kp 2.5 / kd 0.8 / ki 0.02 controller, which is the cleanest current baseline.

Changes from iteration 3: (1) base_speed 1.1 to 1.3. Iteration 3 showed that the slower speed hurt bend progress, and iteration 1 at 1.3 finished the oval in 1.89 s, which leaves margin for the 3 s limit. (2) kd 0.8 to 1.0. Higher damping should reduce the swing that carries the robot across the 0.06 m limit on the bends. kp stays at 2.5 and sensor_size stays at 0.012, so this is a single-variable change on the controller relative to the sensor and speed setup. Geometry, span and weights are otherwise unchanged from iteration 3.

Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress above 0.3, with max_error falling toward 0.05 m. Oval should still finish in about 1.9 s. Hypotheses: (a) the bend overshoot is damping-limited, so kd 1.0 should cut max_error on the s-bend; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 on the oval, kd is too high; (c) if slalom progress stays near 0.1 with line_loss_events near 1, the limit is line loss at the bend entry, and the next lever is sensor y position or line_loss mode. Measurements wanted: per-track completion, progress, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and completion_time.
